bihar_raw_news.title: Valmiki Tiger Reserve to Become Bihar's Vulture Conservation Hub - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next Valmiki Tiger Reserve to Become Bihar’s Vulture Conservation Hub 19 Oct 2026 3 min read Why in News ? Valmiki Tiger Reserve (VTR) , located in West Champaran district of Bihar, has started vulture conservation efforts in the Gonauli forest range . If developed as planned, it will become India’s 9th vulture conservation and breeding centre. Key Points About Vultures: They are large scavenging birds of prey found across the world except Antarctica and Australia. The 23 species are classified into Old World vultures (Europe, Asia and Africa) and New World vultures (the Americas), which evolved independently through convergent evolution. Diet and Ecological Role : Primarily feed on carrion, preventing the spread of pathogens, reducing decomposition-related pollution and maintaining ecosystem health. Some species eat fruits, eggs or bones. Adaptations : Strong stomach acid and resistance to pathogens help them digest decaying carcasses. Many have bald heads that facilitate hygiene. Behaviour and Reproduction: Some cool themselves through urohidrosis (defecating on their legs). Many species are monogamous, with both parents caring for their young. Threats : Poisoning, habitat loss, electrocution and food scarcity threaten vulture populations. Vulture populations declined significantly primarily due to veterinary diclofenac , which causes kidney failure. India banned its veterinary use in 2006 and has undertaken captive breeding and conservation measures. Valmiki Tiger Reserve Valmiki Tiger Reserve (VTR) in West Champaran, north-western Bihar, represents the Himalayan Terai landscape, characterised by rocky hills, doon valleys, rivers, streams, alluvial plains, swamps and grasslands. Covering approximately 901.07 sq. km, it comprises Valmiki National Park and Valmiki Wildlife Sanctuary. The Gandak River forms the western boundary of the sanctuary, while the Sonha and Pachnad rivulets join it at Valmikinagar to form the sacred Triveni confluence. Known as the Narayani in Nepal, the Gandak is a major river of the region. The Harha–Masan river system originates in the Valmiki forests and contributes to the Burhi Gandak River system downstream. The Pandai River flows from Nepal into Bihar and joins the Masan. These rivers and their tributaries sustain the reserve’s diverse ecosystems and serve as major sources of water. bihar_raw_news.content: The Bihar Combined Entrance Competitive Examination Board (BCECEB) has released the seat matrix for the Stray Vacancy Round—the final counselling phase of UGMAC 2026. This document lists all remaining vacant MBBS and BDS seats across government and private medical colleges in Bihar. If you did not secure a seat in the first three rounds or chose to participate in this final opportunity, this is your last chance to claim a medical seat in the state. The matrix is now live on the official BCECEB portal, and candidates must review it carefully before filling their choices. The Stray Round is your final opportunity to secure an MBBS or BDS seat in Bihar; download the seat matrix from bceceboard.bihar.gov.in, check vacancies in your category, and submit your choices before the deadline. Unlock My College List What Is the Stray Round and Why Does It Matter? The Stray Vacancy Round is the fourth and final phase of UGMAC 2026 counselling. It fills seats that remain unfilled after the first three regular rounds of allotment and candidate reporting. Once this round closes, any remaining vacancies in Bihar's state quota cannot be filled again—they are lost for that academic year. For aspirants who did not secure a seat earlier or who wish to upgrade to a better college or course, the Stray Round represents the absolute last window. Participation requires fresh online consent and adherence to the BCECEB deadline for choice submission. Missing this opportunity means waiting another year to pursue MBBS or BDS in Bihar. Of the MBBS seats, 501 were in private medical colleges and 117 were in government institutions across 14 colleges. These numbers represent seats that candidates either did not fill, rejected, or failed to report for after allotment. The actual Stray Round vacancies will be lower than these Round 3 figures, as some seats will have been filled during Round 3 reporting. The official seat matrix now published shows the exact current vacancies by college, course, and reservation category. Government colleges held seats across all major categories: 57 unreserved, 24 backward class, 14 extremely backward class, 11 economically weaker section, 7 scheduled tribe, and 3 scheduled caste positions. Lord Buddha Koshi Medical College in Saharsa offered 46 general MBBS seats, representing a significant opportunity for unreserved category candidates. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar's GI-tagged Mithila Makhana expands global footprint, exports cross 7,000 tonnes
bihar_raw_news.content: ANI Union Minister Piyush Goyal highlighted the international success of Bihar's GI-tagged Mithila Makhana in a recent post. New Delhi: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal has said Bihar 's GI-tagged Mithila Makhana is winning hearts worldwide, highlighting its nutritional benefits, versatility and growing international reach. In a social media post, Goyal described Mithila Makhana as a superfood and credited farmers for their contribution to its growing popularity. He also emphasised the government's efforts to take Bihar's local products to international markets. "Bihar's GI-tagged Mithila Makhana is winning hearts worldwide with its exceptional nutritional benefits, delightful crunch and incredible versatility. Behind this global success is the tireless toil of our hardworking farmers. Together with the efforts of CM@Samrat4BJPji, we are committed to taking Bihar's local treasures to global markets," Goyal said. Makhana, scientifically known as Euryale ferox, is an aquatic crop grown mainly in shallow ponds, lakes and wetlands. Its seeds are processed or roasted and popped to produce the edible fox nuts commonly consumed as a snack. According to Ministry of Commerce data, India exported more than 7,000 metric tonnes of makhana and value-added makhana products to over 20 international destinations during FY 2025-26. These markets include the United States, the Middle East and Africa. Live Events Bihar accounts for nearly 85 per cent of India's total makhana production , making it the country's leading production centre for the crop. India is the world's largest producer of makhana, with cultivation concentrated mainly in Bihar, West Bengal and Assam. The product has expanded beyond its traditional consumption in Bihar, supported by growing health awareness, startups developing value-added products and the increasing involvement of Farmer-Producer Organisations (FPOs). To strengthen the sector, a separate Harmonised System (HS) code for makhana came into effect in July 2025 under the Finance Bill, 2025. The separate classification provides a distinct trade code for the product. The government has also taken steps to modernise the sector. The National Makhana Board was announced in the Union Budget 2025-26 and formally launched in Bihar on September 15, 2025. Additionally, the government has approved a Central Sector Scheme for the Development of Makhana with a total outlay of Rs 476.03 crore for 2025-26 to 2030-31. The scheme aims to support research and innovation, improve the availability of quality seeds, strengthen farmers' skills, upgrade harvesting and post-harvest practices, promote value addition and branding, expand marketing and exports, and improve quality control. Under the scheme, Rs 30 crore was approved for 2025-26 and Rs 90 crore for 2026-27. Add as a Reliable and Trusted News Source Add Now! bihar_raw_news.title: ESY 2026–27 ethanol tender: Has India abandoned its maize farmers to promote lowest ex ...
bihar_raw_news.content: All News English Ethanol News Top News Trendings Dr. CK Jain, President, Grain Ethanol Manufacturer’s Association The latest ethanol tender threatens to undermine maize cultivation, intensify competition for food grains and reverse years of efforts to build a sustainable industrial-grain economy. The Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) have invited bids for 1,100 crore litres of ethanol for ESY 2026–27. However, the procurement framework raises fundamental questions about India’s agricultural priorities, food security and long-term industrial development. With sugarcane juice, sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses excluded from the tender, almost the entire ethanol requirement will now have to be met through grain-based feedstocks, apart from limited contributions from C-heavy molasses and other permitted sources. Last year, approximately 289 crore litres were initially allocated to sugarcane-based feedstocks. This substantial demand must now shift to alternative sources, principally grains. Excess Capacity and the Lowest-Price Trap Against an ethanol requirement of 1,100 crore litres, industry expectations suggest that suppliers could offer capacity more than twice the requirement. The tender prescribes different procurement prices for different feedstocks. With substantial oversubscription expected, producers will face intense pressure to secure allocations, making the lower-priced feedstock categories particularly attractive, even where production economics are challenging. With FCI rice availability limited, damaged food grains (DFG), particularly broken rice, could emerge as a major source of supply at Rs 64 per litre, compared with Rs 68.86 for maize-based ethanol. Industry expectations suggest DFG and broken-rice ethanol volumes could increase from approximately 80 crore litres last year to over 700 crore litres. This raises an obvious question: where will such enormous quantities of broken rice come from? Under India’s biofuel policy, damaged food grains include broken rice and food grains unfit for human consumption. However, broken rice is not necessarily damaged or unfit for food. It is widely consumed and used in food processing and animal feed. A massive expansion of ethanol demand for these grains could create direct competition between food, feed and fuel, pushing grain prices sharply higher and contributing to food inflation. The government may save a few rupees per litre on ethanol procurement, only to impose a much larger cost on consumers through higher food prices. Why Would Farmers Continue Growing Maize? Since 2023, the government has actively promoted maize as an industrial grain for ethanol production, providing incentivised ethanol pricing and organising campaigns to encourage farmers to shift from water-intensive crops such as paddy. Yet the latest tender reduces the maize ethanol incentive from Rs 5.79 to Rs 2.79 per litre, bringing its procurement price down to Rs 68.86. bihar_raw_news.title: Lower sugar production and ethanol policy shift put Indian sugar mills in focus - ChiniMandi
bihar_raw_news.content: All News English Ethanol News Indian Sugar News Sugar News Top News AI Representational Image India’s sugar industry is facing a challenging supply outlook as production is expected to decline this season, while a change in ethanol procurement rules has altered the role of sugar-based feedstocks in the biofuel market, CNBC TV18 reported. Oil marketing companies (OMCs), including Indian Oil Corporation (IOC), Bharat Petroleum Corporation (BPCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation (HPCL), have invited bids for 1,100 crore litres of ethanol for the 2026-27 season. However, the tender excludes ethanol produced from sugarcane juice, sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses. Instead, OMCs are seeking ethanol supplies from C-heavy molasses, maize, broken rice and surplus rice from the Food Corporation of India (FCI), among other eligible feedstocks. The exclusion comes at a time when India’s sugar production is expected to fall, raising questions about the availability of sugar and the allocation of sugarcane between sugar production and ethanol. The change in procurement rules could also influence mills’ operational decisions, depending on the economics of sugar and ethanol production. India’s sugar production is estimated at 27-29.5 million tonnes in the current season, compared with around 31 million tonnes last year. Domestic consumption is projected at 28.5-29 million tonnes, leaving a narrow gap between production and demand. Below-normal monsoon conditions have raised concerns over sugarcane yields, particularly in Maharashtra and Karnataka, two of the country’s largest sugar-producing states. Estimates indicate that sugar output across the two states could decline by around 14-19%. Production prospects are relatively better in Madhya Pradesh and some northern states. However, the expected decline in Maharashtra and Karnataka has increased concerns over overall domestic sugar availability. Sugar prices have already strengthened in recent months, supported by concerns over lower crop output and tighter supplies. Festival-season demand has added to the pressure on the domestic market, while concerns over global availability have also supported prices. India has achieved its target of 20% ethanol blending in petrol, with grain-based feedstocks accounting for a significant share of ethanol supplies. Maize has contributed around 42% of ethanol supplies in recent years, while surplus rice accounted for 22% and damaged food grains for 7%. Together, these grain-based sources represented around 71% of the feedstock mix, compared with approximately 25% from sugarcane-based sources. With sugar production expected to remain under pressure and sugar-based ethanol excluded from the latest procurement tender, mills will have to assess their production mix in line with domestic sugar requirements, ethanol economics and the prevailing procurement policy.

bihar_raw_news.title: National conference in Pune on Nov 2 on water security of sugar factories and ethanol ...
bihar_raw_news.content: All News English Indian Sugar News Sugar News AI Representational Image A national conference has been organised in Pune on Nov 2, 2026, to find solutions to the water crisis facing sugar factories and ethanol projects due to the drought situation in the state, dwindling water storage in dams, and falling groundwater levels, Punyanagari reported. The conference will be held in the main auditorium of COEP in Shivajinagar in collaboration with the Sugar Commissionerate of the Govt. of Maharashtra, Indian Federation of Green Energy, and COEP Technological University, informed Dilip Patil, Regional Director, IFGE-West Pune. The inaugural session of this conference will be attended by the State Cooperation Minister Babasaheb Patil. Maharashtra Sugar Commissioner Dr Sanjay Kolte, President of Western Region Atul Kharate, Former Sugar Commissioner Shekhar Gaikwad, VSI Director General Sambhaji Kadu Patil, and either the Vice Chancellor or the Director of COEP Technological University will be present on this occasion. This conference will focus on reducing dependence on fresh water by collecting, purifying, and reusing the evaporation condensate water generated in the factories, as the drought affects the crushing season of many sugar factories. If there is a shortage of water, it can lead to disruptions in production and even premature closure of factories. The sugar industry in Maharashtra is an important pillar of the rural economy. Along with sugar production, co-generation, distillery, ethanol, and bio-CBG projects are transforming the nature of sugar factories into integrated bioenergy complexes. However, all these processes require a large amount of water. Therefore, continuing the operations of these industries in drought conditions is becoming a big challenge.

bihar_raw_news.title: AI infra boom faces data center financing risks - ET Datacenters
bihar_raw_news.content: Investments & Deals 1 min Read AI infra boom faces data center financing risks Goldman Sachs highlights growing financing risks in the expanding artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure sector, particularly concerning data centre bonds. Investors should assess individual projects for potential risks before investing, amidst rising demand for computing capacity. ETDatacenters Published On Oct 19, 2026 at 01:10 PM IST Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Bookmark Comment Highlights Goldman Sachs highlights financing risks in AI infrastructure and data centre bonds. High-yield data centre bonds face pressure as investors assess expansion risks. Investors must evaluate individual projects for construction, repayment, and regulatory risks. Power availability and insurance are critical factors for project viability. Goldman Sachs research indicates increasing concerns about financing artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, questioning whether credit markets can sustain the massive investments required for data centres. High-yield bonds issued by data centre companies are facing pressure as investors evaluate the risks of rapid AI infrastructure expansion, the report stated. Amanda Lynam from Goldman Sachs' credit research team emphasised that investors must examine construction risks, loan repayment ability, refinancing requirements, and claims against tenants when assessing data centre projects. She also cited power availability , regulatory approvals , and insurance as crucial factors affecting project viability . The report stressed that financial risks need individual project-level assessment, rather than assuming all AI infrastructure investments carry similar risks. This individual assessment approach is also vital for equity investors as companies across sectors increase their exposure to data centres, potentially taking on higher investment risks . The report mentioned Spanish renewable energy company Solaria 's data centre deal in Uruguay as an example of the link between energy firms and data centre infrastructure. Goldman Sachs analyst Alberto Gandolfi believes the risks associated with the Solaria deal are skewed to the upside, with further announcements possible at its capital markets day in November. national_raw_news.title: Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar for 2024 & 2025 conferred on 106 young artists in perform...
national_raw_news.content: Union Culture and Tourism Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat today said that the vision of Viksit Bharat cannot be realised through good infrastructure and materialistic progress alone, but art, culture and heritage will play a vital role in it. Addressing the Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puruskar Ceremony in New Delhi, the Minister said that the soul and true identity of India lies in its cultural traditions and heritage. Mr Shekhawat said that the country is undergoing an era of transformation, with its identity and stature gaining recognition across the world. He noted that artists have a significant role to play in this transformation. The Minister highlighted the contribution of generations of artists who have sustained India’s cultural traditions despite many hardships. Mr Shekhawat conferred the Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar by the Sangeet Natak Akademi for the years 2024 and 2025 to 106 young artists from across the country in the field of performing arts. Rajasthan’s Akram Khan Behrupiya received the puraskar for folk dance, Bihar’s Manisha Srivastava for Folk music, while Hito Kiho from Nagaland was honoured for Choir music. Subhashree Swain was conferred the puraskar for Chhau dance and Ghanshyam Sahu was given the award for Playwriting. Talking to Akashvani News, theatre actor and director Dr Anand Kumar Pandey expressed his happiness over his achievement. He said that theatre is a lifelong commitment and is determined to continue contributing to the field of acting, direction and writing. Dr Pandey said that he is working towards creating better opportunities for emerging artists across Chhattisgarh.

national_raw_news.title: French President Macron rejects Interior Minister Laurent Nunez’s resignation amid protests...
national_raw_news.content: French President Emmanuel Macron has expressed concern over security failures that led to violent protests across the country but rejected the resignation of Interior Minister Laurent Nunez amid the crisis. According to local media reports, at least 2,400 people have been arrested following the unrest, during which town halls were set on fire and hundreds of businesses were looted or damaged. The Elysee Palace, the official residence of the president of France, said Nunez had submitted his resignation yesterday, but the President refused to accept it, citing the need for continued leadership of law enforcement during the crisis. Macron directed the Interior Minister to ensure transparency over the planning and intelligence failures that led to the violence and introduce new operational methods for security forces. The protests followed calls by labour unions, student organisations and activists. According to local media, authorities estimated that around 5 Lakh 50 thousand people took part in Saturday’s largely peaceful marches, while organisers put the figure at 8 Lakh. On Sunday, Macron expressed anger and shame over the rioting and looting during nationwide demonstrations. The French President also announced measures to address economic concerns, including rising fuel prices and the cost of living, and pledged firm legal action against those involved in the violence.

national_raw_news.title: Telangana Governor attends Saddula Bathukamma celebrations in Hyderabad 4 hours ago 71
national_raw_news.content: Telangana Governor Shiva Pratap Shukla has said Telangana is the birthplace of dreams. The Governor and his wife attended the Saddula Bathukamma celebrations on Tank Bund on Sunday as chief guests. He extended heartfelt greetings to Telangana people at home and abroad. He described Bathukamma as a living symbol of Telangana’s rich cultural heritage, women’s strength and deep reverence for nature. He praised the mothers and sisters who have preserved this tradition for generations. Referring to global climate challenges such as El Niño, the Governor noted that the state has received lower rainfall this year. He called it a clear warning and cautioned that indiscriminate use of natural resources could lead to a severe water crisis. The Governor said protecting nature and water is the truest form of worship. He urged every citizen to treat water conservation as a first duty rather than only a government responsibility and to stop water wastage immediately. He stressed rainwater harvesting, protection of tanks and ponds, and recharging of groundwater. He also appealed to farmers to give priority to crops that need less water and suit local conditions. Ministers Jupally Krishna Rao and Seethakka also spoke on the significance of the festival. Film actors Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika, consuls general of the United States and Germany, and senior officials took part.
